::: {.page-intro}
**Make real code faster, and prove it.** In groups of **2–3**, take code from a real project
(ENSAI, personal, or open source), speed up one or several of its building blocks, and
**measure precisely what you gained**.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="In a nutshell"}
- **Groups** of 2–3, on an ENSAI, personal, or open-source project.
- **Deliverables**: a **report (~8 pages)** and a **30-minute presentation**.
- **Before you start**: a short proposal with a first timing.
:::

## The task

1. **Present the project** briefly, and how the code runs overall.
2. **Find where the time goes**, and pick the blocks worth optimizing.
3. **Optimize them**: parallelize, change the code, or both. The course's tools apply here: compiled or vectorized loops, concurrency and parallelism without sharing, memory locality, batching, and the GPU.
4. **Measure the speedup**, on the block and on the whole program.

Choose code that runs long enough to measure and gives a result you can check. Before you start, send a **short proposal**: the project, the block you target, and a first timing ([example below](#example-proposal)).

## Deliverables

- A **report** of about **8 pages**.
- A **30-minute presentation**, questions included, in which every member speaks.

## Reproducibility and proposed grading

Submit runnable code (script or notebook), dependencies/versions and a short command or cell sequence
that reproduces the comparison. Record input size/type, hardware, workers/BLAS threads, warmup,
repetitions, included costs and the correctness check. Synthetic inputs are fine for confidential projects.
Report both block and whole-program timings; a well-explained slowdown is a valid finding.

| Criterion | Weight |
|---|---:|
| Correctness and validation | 25% |
| Measurement protocol and reproducibility | 30% |
| Diagnosis and justification | 25% |
| Clear report and presentation | 20% |

The initial proposal states the input, result to preserve, first whole-program timing, target block,
hypothesis and available hardware. Project preparation and the **30-minute presentations are outside
the nine teaching hours** (30 minutes × number of groups). The ~8-page report format is unchanged.

## Example proposal {#example-proposal}

An invented case, to show the expected level. **The numbers are illustrative, not measurements.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Project** | Bootstrap confidence intervals for a regression estimator (Python, NumPy). |
| **Input** | 50,000 rows × 20 columns, 2,000 resamples, fixed seed. |
| **Result to preserve** | The interval bounds, compared with a tolerance of 10⁻⁸ for the same seeds. |
| **First timing** | Whole program 212 s; the resampling loop 187 s (88 %). Laptop, 8 cores, 1 BLAS thread, median of 3 runs after one warmup run, data loading included. |
| **Target block** | The resampling loop: each resample refits the model independently. |
| **Hypothesis** | Resamples share nothing, so they can run in separate processes, each returning its estimates. With 88 % of the time in the block, 8 workers give at most 1 / (0.12 + 0.88 / 8) ≈ 4.3× on the whole program. |
| **Next measurement** | Whole-program and block times for 1, 2, 4, 8 workers, pool startup included; per-worker seeds so the result can be checked. |
| **What could go wrong** | Each fit already uses several BLAS threads; copying the data to every worker costs more than expected. Either would be reported and explained. |

What makes it a good proposal: a result that can be checked, a timing of the **whole** program,
a block chosen **because** it dominates, a hypothesis that predicts a number, and a measurement
that could contradict it.

## Rules

- **Any language**: Julia, Python, or another one.
- **Optimized libraries are allowed**, as long as you explain why they are faster.
- **AI assistants are allowed**, if you say what you used them for.
- **Confidential projects**: run the block on synthetic data of the same size.

*Dates are announced in class.*
